title: Use Colored Screen Light for a Deliberate Selfie Look
description: Create a deliberate colored selfie with screen light on iPhone. Control competing room light, preview one tint and check the saved photo.
direct: Pick one screen color and keep competing room light under control. Take a test selfie so you can judge the tint in the saved photo.
figureAlt: A portrait uses a deliberate single-color pink fill rather than neutral lighting.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot or measured export.
cards.decision.heading: Use one tint at a time
cards.decision.body: This is a creative lighting choice. A blue or pink face is not intended to reproduce neutral skin color, and a single phone screen does not promise the two-sided look of a studio with multiple lights.
sections.detail-0-0.heading: Light and a filter do different work
sections.detail-0-0.body: Colored light falls on surfaces before capture, so face shape, nearby objects and shadows influence the result. A later color filter changes an already captured image. Nikon’s lighting lesson demonstrates color control with physical lights and gels; it does not establish that a phone screen has the output or precision of studio equipment.
sections.detail-1-0.heading: Keep the experiment simple
sections.detail-1-0.body: Its current release offers adjustable screen color and brightness while the camera stays open. All light colors can be previewed free, and the first five photos are free; Pro adds unlimited photos and video recording.
sections.detail-1-1.heading: Check the tint in the saved photo
sections.detail-1-1.body: No split-color mode, calibrated output or white-balance lock is claimed here. Ambient light, phone distance and camera processing all matter. Use the saved photo as your check, and choose a different setup if the screen alone cannot produce the look comfortably.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Why does the tint almost disappear near a bright window?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: The room light may overpower the screen. Move to softer light and keep the framing steady while you test again.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Should I raise the screen to maximum brightness?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Use a comfortable setting. Check facial detail and the strongest highlights before increasing it.

steps.step-1.text: Open the front-camera preview in GlowPop: Selfie Glow Camera. Choose one screen-light color and use a comfortable brightness.
steps.step-2.text: Keep the framing steady while adjusting nearby lamps or your position. Compare the tint with and without strong competing room light. Leave enough light to see facial detail.
steps.step-3.text: Take a test photo and inspect the saved result. Adjust the color or brightness if highlights lose detail or the tint overwhelms the expression you want.
